rules.text: Only fire at a robot you saw this turn, with the gun aimed at it.
rules.read_back: Whenever it fires a shot (of any power), there must be a target that was scanned this very turn (age 0) and the gun must be pointing at that target within 3.0°; if there is no target, a stale scan, or the gun is not aimed, it must not fire.
clauses: r.fire matches Some(p) ==> ((obs.target matches Some(t) && t.age == 0) && aimed(*obs))
rules.why: The firing condition (gun_heat == 0, t.age == 0, is_aimed, energy > p) looks like it matches the rule, but Verus could not rule out an arithmetic overflow or underflow in the code, for example in the angle subtractions behind angle_diff or in the 2 * angle_diff(...) overshoot in radar_turn; Verus gave no line number, so this is my reading and the cause is unconfirmed.

deleted_starters.text: Never fire a shot you can't afford.
Never drive toward a wall or building closer than 80 px.

explanation.headline: Not proved: Verus couldn't verify the fire-only-when-aimed rule (S2)
explanation.summary: Verus returned "unknown" for S2 ("Only fire at a robot you saw this turn, with the gun aimed at it"), noting a possible arithmetic underflow or overflow, so the rule is not proved. Neither the open arena nor the city map showed any violation, but that does not make the rule safe, because the proof did not complete.
